findings.title: Untrusted RSS feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML (stored XSS)
findings.body: poll_feed.rb takes `i.content` straight from an externally-controlled RSS/Atom feed, only unescapes HTML entities, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (see app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22). In `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb line 133), raw_html posts skip the normal `PrettyText`/sanitization pipeline entirely (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), so whatever HTML comes from the feed ends up verbatim in `post.cooked`. The embed view then outputs it unescaped (`<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and the normal topic page presumably does the same since `cooked` is generally trusted. A malicious or compromised feed can inject `<script>` tags or other active content that will execute in every visitor's browser (both on the embed page and on the main forum topic page). There is no sanitizer anywhere in this import path (Nokogiri's `absolutize_urls` only rewrites href/src, it doesn't strip scripts/attributes).

findings.title: Use of Kernel#open (open-uri) on externally supplied URLs risks command/file injection
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (Kernel#open via `open-uri`) directly on a URL that is not scheme-validated before this point (the `^https?://` check only happens later, inside `TopicEmbed.import`, which `import_remote` never calls before opening the URL). `Kernel#open` is well known to treat strings beginning with a pipe character (e.g. `|some-shell-command`) as a command to execute, and can also open local files via `file://` or bare paths. `import_remote` is invoked directly with attacker/feed-influenced strings in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, line 148) where `t[:link]` comes from parsing an externally supplied Disqus XML export, and in `lib/topic_retriever.rb#fetch_http` with the user-supplied `embed_url`. While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` provides some protection for the web-triggered path, the thor task has no such guard, and the scheme check inside `import_remote`→`import` happens too late (after `open` has already run). This should use a strict allow-list of schemes (http/https only) and/or `URI.open`/`Net::HTTP` instead of bare `Kernel#open` before performing the request.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring containment instead of exact match
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` only verifies that `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`, rather than verifying the message truly originated from the Discourse host. This is a loose, non-standard way to validate postMessage origins and is fragile: e.g. it does not account for scheme/port differences and can be confused by crafted `discourseUrl` values that happen to contain unrelated but overlapping substrings. The check should parse both values and perform an exact origin comparison (e.g. compare `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin`).

findings.title: Race condition on first-time embed import can raise unhandled RecordNotUnique
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` to decide whether to create a new topic/post or update an existing one. If two requests for the same new `embed_url` run concurrently (e.g. a user request and the hourly feed poller, or two near-simultaneous visitors before the Redis throttle key in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is set), both can see `embed.blank?` as true and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!(...)` with the same `embed_url`. Since `embed_url` has a unique DB index (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), the second `create!` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued anywhere in this path, causing the background job (or request) to fail with an unhandled exception instead of gracefully falling back to the update path.

findings.title: No timeout on blocking HTTP fetch for feed polling (open-uri)
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `open-uri` with no read/open timeout configured. If the configured feed URL is slow, unresponsive, or the connection hangs, this call can block the Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely (or for a very long time), since `sidekiq_options retry: false` won't help here and there is no `Timeout` wrapper. The same issue applies to `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed#import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48). This can starve the scheduled-job queue of workers.

findings.title: feed_key method is defined but never used (dead/incomplete code)
findings.body: `feed_key` computes a Redis key based on a SHA1 of the feed URL (`"feed-modified:#{...}"`), presumably intended to support conditional GETs / tracking last-modified state to avoid re-downloading/re-parsing the whole feed on every run, but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed` or elsewhere in the class. This indicates either dead code that should be removed, or an incomplete feature (feed modification tracking) that was never wired up, which could be confusing for future maintainers and leaves `require 'digest/sha1'` as an otherwise-unused dependency for this half-implemented feature.

findings.title: Third-party gem loaded via require_dependency instead of require
findings.body: `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` loads the Nokogiri gem through Rails' autoload/dependency-tracking mechanism, which is meant for application code that should be reloaded between requests in development, not for third-party native-extension gems. Using `require_dependency` for a gem like Nokogiri is non-idiomatic and can cause Rails to attempt to track/reload it as part of the app's dependency graph, which is unnecessary overhead and can lead to subtle reload issues with native extensions. This should simply be `require 'nokogiri'` (or omitted entirely since Nokogiri is already a Bundler dependency loaded at boot).

findings.title: Unused require_dependency for email/sender
findings.body: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` at the top of this job is never used anywhere in the file (there is no reference to `Email::Sender`). This looks like leftover/copy-paste code and should be removed to avoid confusion about the job's actual dependencies.

findings.title: No test coverage for the actual feed-parsing/import logic in poll_feed
findings.body: The spec for `Jobs::PollFeed` only verifies the guard conditions in `execute` (that `poll_feed` is or isn't called based on site settings) by stubbing out `poll_feed` itself. There is no test exercising the real `poll_feed` method: parsing the RSS/Atom feed with SimpleRSS, falling back from `i.link` to `i.id`, unescaping HTML, or calling `TopicEmbed.import` with the right arguments. Given the security-sensitive nature of this import path (raw HTML is stored and rendered unescaped), and the fact that `open(...)` has no error handling, this is a significant gap — bugs in URL selection, content extraction, or error handling for malformed feeds would not be caught by this test suite.
